title: JSX and Components
subtitle: Create reusable React components and write UI using JSX.
description: Learn JSX syntax, component structure, expressions inside JSX and how React components become reusable building blocks.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 2: JSX and Components. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “JSX and Components”. The goal is to create reusable React components and write UI using JSX.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

React builds user interfaces from components, which are reusable functions that describe what should appear. JSX lets a component express UI with syntax resembling HTML, but it follows JavaScript expression rules and has a few different attribute names.

blocks.question: A component returns two sibling elements with no wrapper. What should be done?
options: Delete one element without considering the design.
Put the elements inside a comment.
Use a CSS selector instead of JSX.
Wrap them in a parent element or fragment.
blocks.explanation: A component needs to return a valid element tree; a fragment groups siblings without an extra DOM node.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A component needs to return a valid element tree; a fragment groups siblings without an extra DOM node.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A component needs to return a valid element tree; a fragment groups siblings without an extra DOM node.

blocks.question: A JSX attribute uses class= on an element. What is the correct React property?
options: className
cssClassOnly
styleName
classnameId
blocks.explanation: React JSX uses className for the HTML class attribute.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. React JSX uses className for the HTML class attribute.

blocks.question: A component’s event handler must run JavaScript. Which syntax passes a handler?
options: onClick="run()"
onClick={run}
click:run
on-click=run()
blocks.explanation: JSX event props receive handler functions; curly braces insert the JavaScript function reference.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. JSX event props receive handler functions; curly braces insert the JavaScript function reference.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. JSX event props receive handler functions; curly braces insert the JavaScript function reference.

blocks.question: A React Development program runs on a teammate’s device but fails on yours. What is the best first debugging step?
options: Rewrite the entire program in another language.
Compare the runtime/compiler, run instructions, and first error message.
Delete the imports and hope it runs.
Change several unrelated lines at once.
blocks.explanation: Environment differences and the first reported error are the most useful starting evidence. Change one thing at a time so the cause remains clear.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Environment differences and the first reported error are the most useful starting evidence. Change one thing at a time so the cause remains clear.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Environment differences and the first reported error are the most useful starting evidence. Change one thing at a time so the cause remains clear.

blocks.question: A new project needs to be maintained by another developer. Which choice helps most?
options: Use a clear entry point, meaningful names, and documented run steps.
Put every instruction on one line.
Use unexplained abbreviations for every name.
Avoid testing because the project is small.
blocks.explanation: Clear structure and reproducible run steps help another developer understand and verify the program.
